Auto profiles the site and chooses the lightest complete pipeline. Classic downloads the entry page and static assets. Smart also crawls bounded same-origin story routes. Browser additionally renders JavaScript and observes runtime/lazy-loaded assets.
Safe performs incremental scroll and clicks only allowlisted, non-form controls while blocking mutation requests and unsafe navigation. Off renders and scrolls but never clicks controls.
Hard ceiling for same-origin routes saved by the archive. It is a safety limit, not a required target.
Maximum route hops from the entry page. Zero archives only the entry route; depth 30 is a practical starting point for large branching stories.
Maximum number of routes opened in the browser engine. Keep this much lower than Max pages because browser rendering is the expensive stage.
Milliseconds to wait after page load, scroll, or safe click so delayed network requests and animations can expose assets.
Maximum incremental scroll operations used to trigger lazy loading. The run stops early when no new content appears.
Maximum allowlisted clicks per runtime page. Login, submit, payment, upload, delete, vote, and similar controls remain blocked.
Stops runtime exploration after this many consecutive rounds discover no new routes, assets, or useful responses.
Use Auto + Safe. Small gallery: 50 pages / depth 10 / runtime 6. Medium story: 300 / 30 / 12. Large story: 800 / 30 / 20, then raise limits only when the manifest reaches a cap.
Choose environment, disabled, or manual routing with common and per-HTTP/HTTPS endpoints, SOCKS4/5, SOCKS5h, credentials, and bypass hosts.
Choose System, Cloudflare 1.1.1.1/1.0.0.1, Google, Quad9, BebasDNS, DoH, DoT, or Custom. A preset synchronizes its endpoint and protocol.
UDP/TCP are unencrypted. DoH uses HTTPS. DoT uses port 853 and requires a hostname so TLS certificate verification remains enabled.
Enabled fallback retries the OS resolver after custom DNS failure. Disable it for fail-closed DNS behavior.
System follows the operating-system route table. Require blocks only downloader traffic when the expected VPN-like interface is absent; it never creates a tunnel.
Checks the saved formats, effective proxy/DNS profile, and local interfaces. It does not fetch a favicon, contact CYOA.CAFE, or send a public resolver test query.

download: Probes the URL before downloading and selects the best engine. Default Auto Output can be Folder or ZIP from Settings.
Stores images as base64 inside one project JSON file. Use this when you want a compact single-file backup.
Creates project.json plus separate image and audio folders inside a ZIP archive.
Creates an embedded JSON and a ZIP package in one run.
Downloads viewer HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, audio, and project data into a playable local folder.
Creates the same website package as ICC Folder, then compresses it into a ZIP archive.
Downloads the visible site without trying to discover a project JSON. Use it for custom viewer formats.
Uses the CYOA-P Vue flow by downloading dist/platform.json and dist/nodes/*.json.
Controls parallel image downloads. Start with 4 to 8 threads for stable hosts.
Wait time after rate-limit responses such as HTTP 429.
Limits download speed in KB/s. Use 0 for unlimited speed.
Downloads fonts referenced by HTML or CSS files.
Uses httpx with HTTP/2 for deep-scan fetches when httpx[http2] is installed.
Downloads YouTube audio with yt-dlp and ffmpeg, then patches local audio paths into the project.
Optional recovery/diagnostic helper. Configure provider and keys from Settings / Maintenance.
Optional fallback for supported gallery/post pages. Open its config from Settings / Maintenance.
Destination folder for all generated files. The folder is created automatically if it does not exist.
The filename is generated from the URL by default, but you can edit it before adding the URL to the queue.
The program writes backup_report.txt, failed_assets.txt, failed_images.txt, and cyoa_downloader.log when relevant.
Download All, Preview, Pause/Continue, Start/Stop Serve, Open Folder, and status/progress are pinned into one compact row.
AI Assist, gallery-dl config, Cloudflare/FlareSolverr, Offline Viewers, and settings import/export live here.
Retry Assets, Retry Images, and Retry Audio are direct compact toolbar buttons.
audio: Scans project JSON for bgmId, direct audio fields, playlists, and YouTube video IDs.
Uses yt-dlp to download YouTube audio, then ffmpeg converts it to MP3.
Rewrites bgmId and useAudioURL so the offline viewer can load local audio files.
Copies the audio folder into the JSON package, ZIP package, or ICC folder as needed.
Writes skipped_youtube_audio.txt when a YouTube track cannot be downloaded.
Searches for ffmpeg in the active PATH.
Reads user and machine PATH entries from the Windows registry.
Checks common winget, Scoop, Chocolatey, and local install locations.
Install ffmpeg and restart the program if audio conversion fails.
Tries browser cookies from Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Chromium, and Safari.
Windows may lock the Chromium cookie database while the browser is open; close Chrome/Edge/Brave completely before retrying, or use an exported cookies.txt.
Export a Netscape cookies.txt with a browser extension, then open Settings / Maintenance → YouTube cookies, choose it, and click Save.
Modern browsers can block autoplay. The offline viewer adds an enable-audio banner when needed.
Click the audio banner once to allow playback on the local page.
queue: Paste a URL and press Enter or click Add. Duplicate URLs are kept as separate jobs.
Edit the filename field below each queued URL before downloading.
Click the mode badge (for example, Auto) on a row and choose another mode. The URL stays in the queue.
Drag the handle at the left of a row to change download priority.
Use the row close button, Remove, or Clear All to manage the queue.
Imports .txt, .csv, .xlsx, or Google Sheet CSV sources with URL, filename, and mode columns.
Click Export List to save the current URL, filename, and mode as CSV or TXT for backup or reuse.
Checks URLs before starting downloads and shows whether project data is likely available.
FOUND means direct project data was detected. JS/SCAN means discovery may require script scanning. ERROR means the URL failed.
Use Proceed with Download to start immediately from the preview results.
Successful URLs are written to download_state.json so a repeated batch can skip completed items.
Adds failed queue items back into the queue.
Uses failed_images.txt to retry image downloads and patch the project JSON.
viewer: Open Viewers and add an offline viewer ZIP such as ICC Plus, ICC Remix, or a compatible custom viewer.
Matches a viewer to the CYOA by reading HTML and script hints.

Each viewer card has an Inject button. Use it to build a playable offline viewer from a project source you already have, even when auto-match did not run. Source can be a file (project.json, app.js, or a zip/rar), a download folder (auto-scans for project.json or app*.js plus images/ and audio/), or a URL (uses the full resolver, including embedded-JS extraction and optional AI). Output is a self-contained <name>_offline folder.
Injects project data into the template marker.
Uses marker-based and balanced-brace injection around the project data placeholder.
Patches project.json fetch calls when the viewer supports local project data.
Adds a floating gear button to offline viewers.
Changes point values in Vuex or Pinia stores.
Removes required fields from rows and objects.
Sets allowedChoices to unlimited across rows.
Selects or deselects all choices in the CYOA.
Use Serve to select a folder and start a local HTTP server.
The browser opens to localhost on the selected server port.
The local server sends permissive CORS headers for local images and audio.
Serve disables browser cache and opens with a cache-busting URL so old CYOAs are not replayed.
Use Stop Server to shut down the local server.
network: Open Settings → Network to configure the complete profile, save it, and validate it offline without requesting a website or public test URL.
Supports environment, disabled, and manual profiles; common or per-HTTP/HTTPS endpoints; HTTP(S), SOCKS4/5, SOCKS5h, and bypass hosts.
Supports system DNS, UDP, TCP, DNS-over-HTTPS, and DNS-over-TLS with custom port, timeout, IPv6, and optional system fallback.
Includes Cloudflare 1.1.1.1/1.0.0.1, Google, Quad9, BebasDNS, DoH, DoT, and a Custom option. Selecting a preset fills the endpoint and protocol.
Uses DNS-over-HTTPS presets without changing Windows, router, browser, or hosts-file settings.
System follows OS routing. Require blocks downloader requests unless an active VPN-like or explicitly named interface is detected; it does not start a VPN.
Validate offline checks formats, effective proxy/DNS state, and local VPN interfaces only. It never downloads a favicon or probes CYOA.CAFE.
Uses httpx HTTP/2 for compatible deep-scan requests.
Writes failed asset details into backup_report.txt when available, otherwise into failed_assets.txt.
Tries normal request first, then cloudscraper, then FlareSolverr when available.
Uses cloudscraper for lighter Cloudflare challenge pages.
Uses a local FlareSolverr service to solve browser-based challenge pages.
Reuse per domain keeps cookies and user-agent for the same host. Clear sessions when cookies become stale.
Inherit proxy sends the app proxy to FlareSolverr. None leaves FlareSolverr on its own network path.
Default. The program never calls gallery-dl.
Uses gallery-dl only for likely post, artwork, gallery, or status pages, not raw CDN images.
Advanced mode. Passes matching URLs to gallery-dl even when the URL shape is uncertain.
Use gallery-dl config for Pixiv OAuth, booru API keys, or account-based extractors.

The CYOA Manager button still shows whether auto-add is enabled.
Use a custom library.sqlite3 path for portable or non-standard installations.
The program checks existing file_path entries before inserting a new library record.
Stores a viewer preference so CYOA Manager can open the project with the correct viewer.
Finds project JSON files larger than 1 KB in a selected folder.
Allows manual multi-select of project JSON files.
Exports projects downloaded in the last session.
Shows counts for added, already existing, and failed items.

Targets window.__pinia.state.value for newer ICC Plus builds.
Injects the overlay before the closing body tag in offline viewer folders.
Deletes requirement arrays from rows and objects.
Marks all objects as not selected.
workflow: Adds the current URL to the queue.
Runs the URL probe without starting a full download.
Starts a local server for a generated ICC folder.
Supports many Neocities, Netlify, Vercel, GitHub Pages, and self-hosted CYOA pages.
Resolves iframe-based CYOA pages when possible.
Can reconstruct original URLs from known CYOA archive patterns.
Supports projects with dist/platform.json and dist/nodes/list.json.
Project data for embedded or ZIP outputs.
Summary of downloaded and failed files.
Full session log written to the output folder.

Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Chromium, then Safari.
Export Netscape cookies.txt with a browser extension, select it in Settings / Maintenance → YouTube cookies, then click Save.

Download All, Preview, Pause/Continue, Start/Stop Serve, Folder, and pinned status/progress.
Diagnostics sits next to Help / Guide so checks are one click away.
Download toggles, Retry Assets, Retry Images, Retry Audio, Settings, Reports Center, and CYOA Manager.

Profiles project data, CYOA.CAFE records, routes, and runtime signals, then chooses the lightest complete pipeline.

Auto profiles the site and chooses the lightest complete pipeline. Classic downloads the entry page and static assets. Smart also crawls bounded same-origin story routes. Browser additionally renders JavaScript and observes runtime/lazy-loaded assets.
Safe performs incremental scroll and clicks only allowlisted, non-form controls while blocking mutation requests and unsafe navigation. Off renders and scrolls but never clicks controls.
Hard ceiling for same-origin routes saved by the archive. It is a safety limit, not a required target.
Maximum route hops from the entry page. Zero archives only the entry route; depth 30 is a practical starting point for large branching stories.
Maximum number of routes opened in the browser engine. Keep this much lower than Max pages because browser rendering is the expensive stage.
Milliseconds to wait after page load, scroll, or safe click so delayed network requests and animations can expose assets.
Maximum incremental scroll operations used to trigger lazy loading. The run stops early when no new content appears.
Maximum allowlisted clicks per runtime page. Login, submit, payment, upload, delete, vote, and similar controls remain blocked.
Stops runtime exploration after this many consecutive rounds discover no new routes, assets, or useful responses.
Use Auto + Safe. Small gallery: 50 pages / depth 10 / runtime 6. Medium story: 300 / 30 / 12. Large story: 800 / 30 / 20, then raise limits only when the manifest reaches a cap.

UDP/TCP are unencrypted. DoH uses HTTPS. DoT uses port 853 and requires a hostname so TLS certificate verification remains enabled.
Enabled fallback retries the OS resolver after custom DNS failure. Disable it for fail-closed DNS behavior.
System follows the operating-system route table. Require blocks only downloader traffic when the expected VPN-like interface is absent; it never creates a tunnel.
Checks the saved formats, effective proxy/DNS profile, and local interfaces. It does not fetch a favicon, contact CYOA.CAFE, or send a public resolver test query.
